newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing rose 0.3% in Jan.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing rose 0.3% in Jan.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK industrial production in January:
MINING/QUARRYING INCLUDING OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION

The consensus forecast was for industrial production to rise by 0.2 percent in January, for a year-on-year rise of 2.7 percent. Manufacturing output was expected to rise 0.3 percent on the month and 1.5 percent year-on-year.
The ONS said that 1996 manufacturing output rose by a revised 0.4 percent compared with 1995. It had originally estimated growth at 0.5 percent.
Total industrial production rose an unrevised 1.2 percent last year from 1995.
The ONS said just over half of the manufacturing industries have shown increases in production in the latest three months compared with the previous three.

The most notable increases were of 2.3 percent in the output of the transport equipment industries, 1.0 percent in the basic metals and metal products industries and 0.5 percent in the output of the pulp, paper, printing and publishing industries.

There were falls of 1.4 percent in the output of textiles, leather and clothing, 1.1 percent in the rubber and plastics products industries and a drop of 0.4 percent in machinery and equipment industries' output.
The ONS said that electricity and gas output was depressed by lower demand in January due to slightly milder weather compared with December.
Coal production fell 2.1 percent in the three months to January compared with the previous three and was 12.3 percent down on the same period a year ago.
Output of the durable goods industries rose by 1.9 percent in the three months to January with output of cars up 3.4 percent, the ONS said.

In the non-durable goods industries, output fell by 0.4 percent in the latest three months with a 0.1 percent rise in food, drink and tobacco output more than offset by a 2.7 percent fall in the output of clothing and footwear and industries and a 0.4 percent drop in output of other non-durable goods.
